title: Toilet Flange Height Solutions: Wax Seal, Shims, and a New Long-Bolt Kit (Ask This Old House)
summary: This Old House’s Ask This Old House episode explains the critical seal beneath a toilet between the toilet flange and the sewer line, detailing typical components, failure modes, and practical DIY solutions for height or wobble issues. The segment covers standard configurations (closet flange, wax seal, bolts), how a floor with rot or raised grades affects sealing, and common strategies to adjust height (flange shims, plywood underlayment). It then introduces an advanced flange kit with longer bolts and integrated wax-seal hardware designed to accommodate significant up- or down- building, including a low-profile mounting method with captive fasteners and a “shock-absorber” style mechanism to preserve a positive seal during installation. The discussion highlights trade-offs, such as the potential need for a plumber for pipe modification versus DIY shim-and-kit approaches, and ends with practical tips on trimming bolts and finishing hardware.

sections.title: Flange basics: components and the wax seal
sections.description: Introduction to the standard toilet flange setup: a PVC (or stainless) closet flange with two bolts and a wax seal, connected to the drain pipe and secured to the building; importance of a tight, wobble-free seal to prevent sewer gas leakage.

sections.description: Introduction of an innovative flange kit that features a flange with a built-in wax seal and longer bolts. The kit uses a bottom-fit structure with a plastic tab to keep parts from flopping as the toilet is lowered, maintaining a positive seal at the bottom and a tight seal at the top. The host demonstrates how bolts can protrude, be trimmed, and capped, and explains that this kit is particularly effective for larger build-ups (about 1 to 1.5 inches), while smaller elevations can still use conventional methods. The discussion contrasts this approach with hiring a plumber for pipe rework.
